log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Raichu

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Tyranitar to immediately contest sun: Prankster Taunt stops Venusaur’s Sleep Powder, while Mega Tyranitar can overwrite Drought and threaten Charizard with Rock Slide. Gholdengo provides a sleep-immune special attacker and strong follow-up. Arcanine offers Intimidate, Snarl, and Fire pressure into the physical and special modes.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s primary plan is Charizard-Y/Venusaur sun, using Chlorophyll-boosted Venusaur and repeated Sleep Powder. Whimsicott’s Grass typing prevents Sleep Powder, and Prankster Taunt is a key anti-sun tool. Mega Tyranitar is a strong Charizard answer but should not be exposed carelessly while Venusaur remains active. Gholdengo’s Good as Gold makes it a reliable sleep/status-resistant option. Milotic’s Rain Dance is vulnerable to losing momentum if Venusaur acts first; use it only when rain can be established proactively.

decisions.rationale: Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur immediately establishes sun/Chlorophyll pressure into the previously shown Whimsicott, Mega Tyranitar, Gholdengo, and Milotic core. Raichu provides Fake Out and Encore disruption, while Kingambit gives a strong late-game answer to Whimsicott and Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: G1 opponent brought Whimsicott, Tyranitar, Gholdengo, Milotic; omitted Arcanine and Basculegion. Whimsicott is Timid Focus Sash Prankster with Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast. Tyranitar is Adamant Tyranitarite with Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick/Protect. Gholdengo is Modest Metal Coat Good as Gold with Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Recover/Protect. Milotic is Calm Leftovers Competitive with Rain Dance/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Protect. Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur sun mode is preferred; respect Prankster disruption, Tyranitar Rock Slide, and Milotic Rain Dance. Do not Intimidate Milotic casually; Good as Gold blocks targeted status such as Sleep Powder.

decisions.rationale: Prankster Taunt shuts down Venusaur’s Sleep Powder and Protect options while Whimsicott remains immune to Sleep Powder. Mega Tyranitar’s spread Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO on Charizard, preserving the best immediate answer to the sun core; Venusaur can then be handled with both opponents’ main threat removed.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Charizard/Venusaur plan is sun plus Chlorophyll Sleep Powder. Whimsicott’s Grass typing blocks Sleep Powder, and Prankster Taunt is the strongest anti-sun disruption. Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide reliably OHKOs Charizard, while Venusaur survives it; avoid exposing Tyranitar to unsupported Grass attacks after Charizard is removed. Gholdengo is a reliable status-resistant pivot because of Good as Gold. Milotic’s proactive Rain Dance is preferable only when it can establish rain before Venusaur acts.

decisions.rationale: Switch Whimsicott to Gholdengo to preserve the position with a status-resistant pivot and immediate pressure on weakened Venusaur, while Mega Tyranitar remains active in sand.

Mega Charizard Y sets sun, enabling immediate Solar Beam and Chlorophyll Venusaur. Solar Beam heavily pressures Tyranitar if it attacks, while Life Orb Sludge Bomb guarantees removing Whimsicott despite Focus Sash after its Prankster action.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s G1 bring was Whimsicott/Tyranitar/Gholdengo/Milotic; Arcanine and Basculegion were omitted. Whimsicott: Timid Focus Sash Prankster, Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast. Tyranitar: Adamant Tyranitarite, Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick/Protect. Gholdengo: Modest Metal Coat Good as Gold; Milotic: Calm Leftovers Competitive. Mega Charizard Y sun plus Venusaur is the preferred mode. Whimsicott can always use Prankster disruption before normal-priority attacks; eliminate it promptly. Mega Charizard Y Solar Beam into Mega Tyranitar is 54.1–92.6%, not a guaranteed OHKO. Life Orb Venusaur Sludge Bomb guarantees OHKOing Whimsicott but Focus Sash can preserve it at 1 HP if it is struck first by another attack. Respect Tyranitar Rock Slide and Milotic Rain Dance; Good as Gold blocks targeted status such as Sleep Powder.

decisions.rationale: Raichu preserves Kingambit for Gholdengo and provides immediate Fake Out, Encore, and Focus Sash utility against Tyranitar’s next turn while Venusaur is still Taunted.
decisions.notebook: G2: Whimsicott’s Focus Sash was consumed and it was removed on turn 1. Tyranitar Mega is Adamant and threatens Charizard heavily with Rock Slide; preserve a non-Charizard endgame. Preferred mode remains Charizard-Y sun plus Venusaur when feasible. Gholdengo’s Good as Gold blocks targeted status. Keep Kingambit healthy as the primary Gholdengo answer; Raichu offers Fake Out/Encore tempo and Lightning Rod into Water teams. Respect Milotic/Basculegion Rain Dance and Arcanine’s Snarl.

decisions.rationale: Make It Rain guarantees the KO on Venusaur while also damaging Raichu. Rock Slide pressures both foes, can flinch either, breaks Raichu’s Focus Sash, and adds useful damage without exposing Tyranitar to a single-target attack.
decisions.notebook: Preserve the anti-sun plan: remove Charizard immediately with Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide, then use Gholdengo as the status-resistant pivot. Against Venusaur plus Raichu, spread pressure from Make It Rain and Rock Slide is strong; prioritize eliminating Venusaur and avoid unsupported Grass attacks into Tyranitar. Whimsicott’s Prankster Taunt is the preferred disruption when available.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur is guaranteed to fall to Gholdengo’s Make It Rain at its current HP, so preserve board value by pivoting Kingambit in. Raichu’s Fake Out reliably moves first and denies Tyranitar’s Low Kick/Rock Slide this turn, giving Kingambit a safe entry while Raichu withstands spread Make It Rain.
decisions.notebook: G2: Whimsicott’s Focus Sash was consumed before it fainted; it revealed Taunt. Mega Tyranitar is Adamant, has Sand Stream, and revealed Rock Slide; it can immediately overwrite Charizard-Y sun. Gholdengo is Modest Metal Coat with Good as Gold and its listed Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Recover/Protect set. Preserve Kingambit as the main Gholdengo answer; Raichu provides Fake Out and Lightning Rod tempo into Water attackers. Opponent’s rain options are Milotic and Life Orb Swift Swim Basculegion; account for Arcanine’s Snarl.

decisions.rationale: Raichu moves before Gholdengo, so Shadow Ball pressures it while avoiding another spread Make It Rain drop. Tyranitar’s super-effective Low Kick is the best chance to remove Kingambit despite Chople Berry; combining attacks prevents passivity against both threats.
decisions.notebook: Preserve the anti-sun plan: remove opposing weather setters immediately with Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide, then use Gholdengo as a status-resistant pivot. Whimsicott’s Prankster Taunt is preferred disruption when available. Against Venusaur plus Raichu, prioritize Venusaur and avoid unsupported Grass attacks into Tyranitar. Track Gholdengo’s Special Attack drops after Make It Rain and avoid unnecessary repeated spread use.

decisions.rationale: Nuzzle Mega Tyranitar before it moves, cutting its Speed below Kingambit and adding full-paralysis odds; Protect preserves Kingambit from the immediate Chople-mitigated but still dangerous Low Kick. This keeps the key Gholdengo answer available while establishing Tyranitar control for the next turn.
decisions.notebook: G2: Whimsicott’s Focus Sash was consumed before it fainted; it revealed Taunt. Mega Tyranitar is Adamant with Sand Stream and Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick/Protect; it can overwrite Charizard-Y sun. Gholdengo is Modest Metal Coat Good as Gold with Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Recover/Protect. Preserve Kingambit as the main Gholdengo answer; its Chople Berry substantially softens Tyranitar Low Kick. Raichu provides Fake Out and Lightning Rod tempo into Water attackers. Opponent’s rain options are Calm Leftovers Milotic (Rain Dance/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Protect) and Adamant Life Orb Swift Swim Basculegion (Rain Dance/Wave Crash/Aqua Jet/Protect); account for Jolly Expert Belt Arcanine’s Snarl.

decisions.rationale: Shadow Ball cleanly removes Raichu from 6%, while Low Kick is the strongest available attack into Kingambit and can KO despite Chople Berry. This also preserves Gholdengo’s current -2 Special Attack rather than using Make It Rain again.
decisions.notebook: Maintain the anti-sun plan: immediately remove opposing weather setters with Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide when present, then use Gholdengo as a status-resistant pivot. Prioritize Taunt on disruptive opposing supports when Whimsicott is available. Against Venusaur plus Raichu, prioritize Venusaur and avoid unsupported Grass attacks into Tyranitar. Track Gholdengo’s Special Attack drops after Make It Rain; avoid unnecessary repeated spread use.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Raichu has little immediate value at this HP, while preserving Kingambit is essential for Gholdengo. Switching to Venusaur keeps a potential defensive resource in play; the reduced-success Protect is still the best way to deny the likely Low Kick/double-target line and retain Kingambit for the endgame.

Shadow Ball cleanly finishes 2% Venusaur while Low Kick targets Kingambit with 4× effectiveness and Chople already accounted for. This removes Venusaur’s disruption and pressures Kingambit after its repeated Protects, while preserving Gholdengo’s remaining Special Attack by avoiding Make It Rain.
decisions.notebook: Anti-sun plan remains effective: remove weather setters with Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide when present, then use Gholdengo as a status-resistant pivot. Prioritize disruptive supports and Venusaur before Raichu; avoid unsupported Grass attacks into Tyranitar. Track Gholdengo’s Make It Rain Special Attack drops and avoid unnecessary repeated spread use.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Kingambit is guaranteed to move before the paralyzed Tyranitar; Iron Head plus Life Orb Giga Drain has a meaningful combined KO chance and, if Venusaur acts, Giga Drain can restore it from critical HP. Removing Tyranitar protects Kingambit, the key Gholdengo answer.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Shadow Ball safely removes Raichu from 6%, while Flare Blitz is guaranteed to KO Kingambit from 70%. This pressures both foes simultaneously; even if Kingambit uses Sucker Punch, full-health Gholdengo should survive, and Raichu cannot prevent its own guaranteed knockout.
decisions.notebook: Anti-sun sequencing worked: eliminate weather setters early, then use Gholdengo as a status-resistant pivot. Prioritize disruptive supports and Venusaur before Raichu when possible. Track Make It Rain’s Special Attack drops and avoid unnecessary repeated spread use. Preserve reliable single-target attacks when they secure clean KOs.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out denies Arcanine’s immediate Fire pressure while Kingambit targets the opposing Gholdengo with its strongest reliable Dark attack. Gholdengo moves before Kingambit, but its -2 Special Attack and resisted options make preserving Kingambit’s attack this turn the priority.
decisions.notebook: G2 revealed: Jolly Expert Belt Flash Fire Arcanine has Flare Blitz, Wild Charge, Snarl, Protect. Modest Metal Coat Good as Gold Gholdengo has Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Recover, Protect. Against this endgame pairing, use Raichu’s Fake Out to deny Arcanine while Kingambit pressures Gholdengo with Dark attacks; preserve Kingambit when possible as the primary Gholdengo answer.

decisions.rationale: Gholdengo is fainted and must pass. Arcanine's Flare Blitz is super-effective and guarantees the KO on Kingambit from 70%, while preserving a reliable single-target finisher over weaker spread or neutral options.
decisions.notebook: Anti-sun sequencing has worked: remove weather setters early and use Gholdengo as a status-resistant pivot when available. Prioritize disruptive support and Venusaur before Raichu. Preserve reliable single-target attacks when they secure clean KOs. Track Make It Rain Special Attack drops and avoid unnecessary repeated spread use.

decisions.rationale: Raichu is fainted. Kowtow Cleave is Kingambit’s strongest neutral damage into Arcanine and is the only productive line if Arcanine does not immediately use Flare Blitz; Protect merely delays the likely KO.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Whimsicott is Timid Focus Sash Prankster with Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast. Mega Tyranitar is Adamant with Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick/Protect. Gholdengo is Modest Metal Coat Good as Gold with Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Recover/Protect. Arcanine is Jolly Expert Belt Flash Fire with Flare Blitz/Wild Charge/Snarl/Protect. Endgame principle: preserve Kingambit against Gholdengo; use Raichu Fake Out to create its attacking turns when possible.

reflections.summary: Won by correctly dismantling the sun mode: Gholdengo’s status immunity and focused damage removed Raichu and Venusaur, while Arcanine finished Kingambit. The four brought were appropriate, and Mega Tyranitar was a suitable weather-control Mega, but it was vulnerable when left exposed to Venusaur and Kingambit.
reflections.adjustment: Against the same preview, keep Mega Tyranitar primarily as a sun-reset/pivot resource rather than repeatedly attacking into Kingambit’s Protect; preserve it through Venusaur pressure and reserve Arcanine to clean up Kingambit. Reassess this four at preview if the opponent shifts heavily toward Tauros/Dragonite instead of sun.
reflections.notebook: Anti-sun sequencing remains effective: remove or overwrite opposing weather early, then use Gholdengo as a status-resistant attacker/pivot. Opponent revealed Raichu with Fake Out, Nuzzle, Encore, Lightning Rod, and Focus Sash; avoid relying on Electric attacks and account for its disruption plus Sash. Kingambit has Protect, Defiant, Chople Berry, and Sucker Punch; pressure it with reliable single-target attacks while expecting Protect and preserve Arcanine for the endgame. Mega Tyranitar is useful for weather control here but should not be left exposed to combined Venusaur and Kingambit pressure. Continue prioritizing Venusaur and disruptive support before Raichu, and track Gholdengo’s Make It Rain Special Attack drops.

reflections.summary: Lost because Charizard-Y’s sun/Fire plan matched poorly into Mega Tyranitar and Flash Fire Arcanine, while the remaining Raichu–Kingambit core traded down and left Kingambit exposed to Arcanine’s Flare Blitz. All four available Pokémon were brought, so the key preview issue was Mega Charizard-Y, not the four selection.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, avoid Mega Evolving Charizard-Y into this revealed Tyranitar/Flash Fire Arcanine composition; prioritize preserving Kingambit for Gholdengo while keeping an answer to Arcanine rather than enabling its Fire damage with sun.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s revealed structure includes Sash Prankster Whimsicott disruption, Mega Tyranitar, Gholdengo, and Flash Fire Arcanine. Mega Charizard-Y/sun is a poor Mega plan into Tyranitar plus Flash Fire Arcanine and can amplify Arcanine’s Fire pressure. Future plan: do not default to Charizard-Y Mega; preserve Kingambit for Gholdengo but avoid leaving it as the final answer to Arcanine.
